tool_arguments.query: Lisa Su AMD CEO compensation fiscal 2026

events.content: Lisa Su AMD CEO compensation fiscal 2026

AMD’s 2026 proxy statement reports that Chair, President and CEO Lisa Su received **$55,161,779 in total compensation for fiscal 2025**; this is the most recently disclosed CEO-pay figure in AMD’s FY2026 proxy, rather than compensation for fiscal 2026 itself. [[1, 2]] 

The reported total comprised **$1,291,258 salary**, **$41,669,390 stock awards**, **$8,951,513 option awards**, **$3,125,430 non-equity incentive compensation**, and **$124,188 in other compensation**; there was no separately reported discretionary cash bonus. [[2]] 

AMD set Su’s annualized base salary at **$1,323,000 effective December 27, 2025**, a **5.0%** increase from $1,260,000 a year earlier. [[1]] 

Her 2025 long-term equity grant had an intended target value of **$33.0 million**, comprising 151,283 target PRSUs and 102,516 options; its **$50.62 million** reported stock-plus-option value reflects ASC 718 grant-date accounting values in the summary compensation table. [[1, 3]] 

The $55.16 million reported compensation was **78% above FY2024’s $30.996 million**, and AMD states that approximately **96%** of its CEO’s target total direct compensation was variable or at risk. [[3, 1]]

Sources:
[S6.1] March 27, 2026 - DEF 14A: Definitive proxy statements — https://ir.amd.com/financial-information/sec-filings/content/0001193125-26-129057/d85856ddef14a.htm
[S6.2] Lisa Su — https://aflcio.org/paywatch/AMD
[S6.3] Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) Executive Compensation: 2026 Proxy Statement — https://gloom.sh/stocks/amd/proxy/2026

tool_arguments.summary:
Gross margin comparison (Q2 FY2027, quarters ending July 2026 for NVIDIA and June 2026 for AMD):
- NVIDIA GAAP gross margin: **75.0%** (source S1.1)
- AMD GAAP gross margin: **54%** (source S2.1)

The ~21-percentage-point gap is driven by NVIDIA's higher-margin Data Center segment (dominant AI‑training/inference revenue with minimal hardware cost) versus AMD's more balanced mix of CPU and GPU sales, which carry lower average margins. NVIDIA's scale, software moat (CUDA), and pricing power in the AI accelerator market sustain its superior gross margin, while AMD's margins reflect competitive pricing in both client and datacenter CPU/GPU markets.
